summary: [FAIL — Blocking] MainContentViewModel implements IDisposable and subscribes to IRefreshOrchestrator.StateChanged in its full DI constructor, but ShellViewModel.Transition() never disposes the outgoing CurrentViewModel. Since IRefreshOrchestrator is a singleton with application lifetime, every disconnect-reconnect cycle permanently roots a stale MainContentViewModel instance (and its transitive transient dependencies: LibraryFoldersViewModel, RefreshIndexViewModel) via the orchestrator's event delegate list. The IDisposable.Dispose() implementation was specifically written to prevent this leak, but there is no caller. Fix-Forward applied: sorted VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.* using directives in Program.cs into alphabetical order (non-behavioral).

comments.note: BLOCKING: ShellViewModel.Transition() does not dispose the outgoing CurrentViewModel. MainContentViewModel subscribes to IRefreshOrchestrator.StateChanged (a strong C# event) in its full DI constructor. When the shell leaves ShellState.Ready (e.g. via DisconnectAsync()), Transition() overwrites CurrentViewModel with no disposal call. The outgoing MainContentViewModel instance remains permanently rooted by the singleton orchestrator's event multicast delegate. On each subsequent Ready transition a new instance is created, stacking up leaked event subscriptions. Stale OnRefreshStateChanged handlers then fire against orphaned VMs, triggering wasted DB queries (GetCountAsync) and UI state mutations on non-displayed VMs. Fix: in ShellViewModel.Transition(), capture the outgoing VM and call (outgoing as IDisposable)?.Dispose() after assigning the new CurrentViewModel. Example: var outgoing = CurrentViewModel; CurrentViewModel = _viewModelFactory(newState); (outgoing as IDisposable)?.Dispose();

Fix-Forward applied: sorted the VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.* using directives in Program.cs into strict alphabetical order (Auth, Database, ExternalTools, Library, Logging, Settings, Theme). Prior order was: Auth, Database, Logging, Settings, ExternalTools, Library, Theme — a pre-existing inconsistency that the Developer noted but preserved. Non-behavioral change; QA validation remains intact.
